sample_unit: eyes fitted (real-world trial); 11,502 lens fitting records for algorithm development

links.outcome: Number of trials to final prescription with vs without AI assistance among clinicians
links.effect: Trials needed decreased significantly for six of seven clinicians (all P<0.01); reduction larger for junior than senior clinicians (0.76±0.60 vs 0.32±0.60, P<0.001). Junior and senior clinicians had comparable outcomes (93.96% vs 94.44%, P=0.864).
links.quote: With the assistance of the AI system, the number of trials required to determine the final prescription significantly decreased for six of the seven participating clinicians (all P <0.01).

screen.reason: The study develops an AI tool for orthokeratology lens prescription and evaluates its real-world clinical implementation by junior and senior clinicians, measuring clinical efficiency and outcomes, but does not test a specific organizational deployment safeguard or practice variation.
